snippet.description:
How did Britain stop Hitler’s seemingly unstoppable air force in 1940? 🔔 Subscribe and join us on this journey around the world → https://bit.ly/WorldView-Documentary

A story of human endeavour, the contest between British and German airforces in 1940 which became a defining point of the Second World War. With unseen footage from the feature film, Battle of Britain, this series provides an unbiased accounts of the events in the skies above Britain. A chronological account of a country preparing to defend itself against a rising empire.

Part 1 – The Few
By May 1940, the die was cast and the war started in earnest. This episode examines the build-up to the Battle of Britain, studying the technological advances that the RAF pioneered, to the start of the Battle itself.  At the heart of the RAF production were two world-class fighters – theHurricane & the Spitfire, able to compete against the best that the Luftwaffe had to offer.

Part 2 – Darkest Hour
This focuses on events from July to early Sept. 1940, where both sides were finding their feet.  The Germans tried initially to bomb British naval shipping with limited success. Three separate attacks in August, targeting RAF airfields were successful – Biggin Hill, North Weald & Kenley were all put out of action – albeit temporarily. Then the Germans made a mistake that ultimately lost them the war.

Part 3 – The Blitz
During the first week of September, Hitler decided to move the bombing strategy away from the airfields, to civilian London. This episode examines the spirit of the Londoners who defied Hitler, and ultimately ended the war in the last weeks of September. The RAF with fewer resources, fewer men & machines had beaten the might of the Luftwaffe.

snippet.title: The Real Boston George Was Far More Dangerous Than The Movie
snippet.description:
George Jacob Jung partied with Pablo Escobar. He cleared $100,000 a day. He helped a single Colombian organization flood America with 85% of its cocaine — and then he died broke in a hospice bed in the same Boston suburb where it all began. This is the real story behind the movie “Blow,” and almost none of it looks like Hollywood told you.

In this deep-dive documentary, we break down the full life of George Jacob Jung, aka “Boston George,” aka “El Americano” — from his working-class childhood in Weymouth, Massachusetts, to a fateful prison cell in Danbury, Connecticut in 1974 where he met a young Colombian-German named Carlos Lehder. Together, they sketched the blueprint for what would become the most efficient cocaine pipeline in American history, running tons of product through Norman’s Cay, a private island in the Bahamas, and into Florida and Georgia.

What you’ll learn in this video:
• How a marijuana smuggler from Manhattan Beach became Pablo Escobar’s American partner
 • The truth about the 1974 Danbury prison cell that changed the global drug trade
 • How Norman’s Cay actually worked as a Bahamas transshipment hub
 • What “Blow” got right and the major characters the film invented or combined
 • The real story of Mirtha Jung, their 1984 divorce, and her road to sobriety
 • Why Kristina Sunshine Jung refused to see her father for decades
 • How George testified against Carlos Lehder in 1987 — and the price he paid
 • The 1994 Topeka, Kansas bust with 1,754 pounds of cocaine and the 60-year sentence
 • What happened to Lehder, Escobar, Mirtha, and Kristina after the empire collapsed
 • Why George died in 2021 with nothing but a memoir, a movie, and a daughter he barely knew

Key figures: 
George Jung, Carlos Lehder, Pablo Escobar, Mirtha Calderon Jung, Kristina Sunshine Jung, the Medellín Cartel.

Timeline: 
1942 (birth) → 1968 (marijuana smuggling begins) → 1974 (Danbury prison) → 1976-1984 (cocaine empire peak) → 1987 (testifies vs. Lehder) → 1994 (final arrest) → 2014 (released) → 2021 (death).

This story matters because it shows how America’s cocaine epidemic wasn’t a foreign invasion — it was a partnership. And the contractor always pays.

 • The New York Times obituary, May 9, 2021 (nytimes.com/2021/05/09/us/george-jung-dead.html)
 • The Patriot Ledger, Weymouth, MA reporting (patriotledger.com)

Brazil is said to be a sleeping giant waking up to become one of the world leaders. Our film will tell the country’s history through the eyes of two families over several generations.

In one of the families, the slaves of before became domestic workers, and the former domestics are now employees, with fixed hours and living in their own homes, where they raise their own children rather than those of their bosses. They have reached the middle class. The other family descends from coffee barons and army generals. It is still a wealthy family, but yesterday’s fortune was lost. Its members have witnessed many historical events. These two families will embody the evolutions of Brazil since the twenties until today. Our goal is to intersect the families saga and the nation’s history with a broad range of photo and film archives, both public and private. We will complete this with a more global contextualization of the general History of the country.

snippet.title: Meyer Lansky — The Mob's Financial Architect
snippet.description:
The man known to history as Meyer Lansky was born Maier Suchowljansky on the 4th of July, 1902, in the Russian Empire — a Jewish boy who fled the pogroms and grew up to become the financial mastermind of American organized crime. He was not a brute. He ordered no men gunned down for the cameras and cultivated no celebrity. His weapon was his mind: a genius for numbers, for organization, and above all for money — how to make it, how to move it, and how to hide it.

This documentary traces his full story — the immigrant childhood on the Lower East Side, the lifelong friendship with Lucky Luciano, the Bugs and Meyer Mob, building the architecture of the national syndicate, the glittering casino empire of 1950s Havana, his pioneering of modern money laundering, Castro's revolution, the failed flight to Israel, and a quiet death in Miami Beach — leaving behind a vanished fortune that has never been found.

snippet.title: He Crossed Philadelphia’s Mob — Then They Executed His Whole Family
snippet.description:
He was a hustler, fixer, nightclub owner, political candidate, and underworld broker who thought he could stand between Philadelphia’s street mob and New York’s Mafia. But Major Coxson crossed the wrong people, and the punishment did not stop with him. They came into his Cherry Hill home before sunrise and tried to wipe out everyone inside.

On June 8, 1973, four men arrived at Major Coxson’s house on Barbara Drive in Cherry Hill, New Jersey. They were not strangers. They were let inside because Coxson believed they were friends. Minutes later, the house turned into an execution room. Coxson was bound and shot. His companion Louise Luby was killed. Her daughter Lita was killed. One child escaped through a sliding door and ran to a neighbor for help.

This was not just another street murder. Coxson was connected to Muhammad Ali, Angelo Bruno, Frank Matthews, Camden politics, Philadelphia clubs, and the city’s most dangerous underworld players. He lived like a celebrity, campaigned like a politician, and moved like a gangster. But when a massive heroin deal collapsed, the men around him believed he had cost them money, power, and respect.

What you will learn in this documentary:
How Major Benjamin Coxson rose from car lots and street hustles to Philadelphia underworld power
Why he became known as one of the city’s flashiest Black crime figures
How Coxson built connections with politicians, athletes, nightclub owners, and mob bosses
Why Muhammad Ali called him the future mayor of Camden
How Coxson became a bridge between Philadelphia’s mob world and New York narcotics suppliers
The real connection between Angelo Bruno, Frank Matthews, and Philadelphia’s street rackets
Why the Black Mafia allegedly blamed Coxson for a failed heroin deal
How a political candidate ended up targeted like a mob boss
The June 8 1973 Cherry Hill home invasion that shocked New Jersey
Why Louise Luby and her daughter Lita were killed with him
How a young survivor escaped and helped expose what happened inside the house
Why Ronald Harvey and Samuel Christian became the main names linked to the murder
Why the Coxson case remains one of the most disturbing unsolved mob stories in Philadelphia history

Key figures:
Major Benjamin Coxson, Louise Luby, Lita Luby, Muhammad Ali, Angelo Bruno, Frank Matthews, Samuel “Beyah” Christian, Ronald Harvey, Stanley Branche, Angelo Errichetti, Elijah Muhammad, Philadelphia Black Mafia

Timeline:
1930 birth of Major Benjamin Coxson, 1950s rise through car lots and street rackets, 1960s nightclub and business expansion in Philadelphia, 1968 meeting with Muhammad Ali, 1970 Ali publicly praises Coxson after the Jerry Quarry fight, 1972 Coxson runs for mayor of Camden, early 1973 heroin dispute escalates between Philadelphia and New York underworld figures, June 8 1973 Coxson and members of his household are attacked in Cherry Hill, June 1973 Ronald Harvey becomes a suspect, December 1973 Samuel Christian appears on the FBI Ten Most Wanted list, 1974 Harvey is arrested, 2016 Samuel Christian dies without being convicted in the Coxson murder.

Why this story matters today:
The Major Coxson case shows how Philadelphia’s underworld was never simple. It was not just Italian Mafia families in suits or street crews fighting over corners. It was politicians, celebrity friendships, heroin pipelines, religious fronts, nightclub money, and violent organizations all crossing paths. Coxson tried to move between all of those worlds, but when one deal went wrong, the response was total terror. His murder proved that in Philadelphia’s mob world, being connected to everyone could still save you from no one.

December 7th, 1980. John Lennon is murdered outside the Dakota in New York City. 2,000 miles south, a 31 year old Colombian cocaine trafficker pops champagne and calls it a victory. His name was Carlos Lehder, and the Hollywood film Blow spent two hours making sure you’d never learn the truth about who he really was.

What you’ll learn in this episode:
- How Lehder met George Jung in a Danbury, Connecticut federal prison in 1974 and drafted the entire Medellin Cartel smuggling model from a cell
- How he bought Norman’s Cay in the Bahamas in 1978 and terrorized its residents with armed guards, dobermans, rapes, and machine guns
- The 88,000 dollar monthly cash payment Lehder allegedly delivered to Bahamian Prime Minister Lynden Pindling every 22nd of the month
- The neo Nazi political party Lehder founded in Colombia called the Movimiento Latino Nacional, and his open praise of Adolf Hitler
- His 1987 extradition, the first major narco ever sent to the United States under the new treaty
- The 3.3 ton single shipment that helped earn him life plus 135 years
- His 1991 deal to testify against Panamanian dictator Manuel Noriega
- George Jung’s own 1994 cooperation deal, the part Blow refused to show you
- Lehder’s quiet 2020 release from federal prison and his current life in Bonn, Germany

Carlos Lehder, George Jung, Pablo Escobar, Jorge Ochoa, Lynden Pindling, Manuel Noriega

To ensure a successful landing, he sought to lure the British naval forces away from the English Channel. After several failed attempts to draw Collingwood's and Nelson's fleets to the West Indies, Admiral de Villeneuve allowed himself to be trapped off Cádiz, near Cape Trafalgar, hoping to draw the British there. But he soon received a counter-order and was forced to move to the Mediterranean. Two days after leaving the harbor, on October 21, 1805, the French ships commanded by Villeneuve were intercepted by twenty-seven English ships led by the flamboyant Admiral Nelson...A gripping military and human story with a face-off between two admirals who were complete opposites.

snippet.title: The Real Story of Unbroken - What Happened AFTER The Movie? | Our History
snippet.description:
Unbroken tells the tale of American hero Louis Zamperini, a man who had transformed himself from a child delinquent to a 5,000 metre finalist in the 1936 Olympics. At the outbreak of World War Two, Zamperini joined a bomber crew only to be involved in a near-fatal plane crash. He survived for 47 days adrift, only to be sent to a Japanese prisoner of war camp where he suffered torture and humiliation at the hands of a camp guard nicknamed 'The Bird'. What the movie doesn't show is that Zamperini found God and embarked on an extraordinary journey to forgive his former captors - even the Bird. It is this inspiring tale of redemption and forgiveness that is the real story of Louis Zamperini.

snippet.title: Stewart Granger: Wie der Hollywood-Held einsam und vergessen starb
snippet.description:
Er ritt durch Afrika, kämpfte mit dem Schwert, jagte Löwen und heiratete eine Prinzessin – und trotzdem starb Stewart Granger einsam und weitgehend vergessen. Wie konnte einer der größten Stars des goldenen Hollywood-Zeitalters in einem leeren Restaurant in Beverly Hills enden?
 
In diesem Video erzählen wir die ganze Geschichte des Mannes, der einst die Leinwand beherrschte – von seinen Anfängen in London über den Skandal seiner Ehe mit Jean Simmons, den Konflikt mit dem mächtigen Howard Hughes, den weltweiten Erfolg mit „König Salomons Schatz" und „Scaramouche", bis hin zu den deutschen Karl-May-Filmen wie „Old Surehand" und „Unter Geiern", die ihn dem deutschsprachigen Publikum besonders nahebrachten.
 
Doch hinter dem Glanz lag ein anderes Leben. Drei Ehen, die zerbrachen. Kinder, die ohne ihren Vater aufwuchsen. Eine Karriere, die langsam verblasste. Und ein Geständnis kurz vor seinem Tod, das alles in einem anderen Licht erscheinen lässt.
 
Stewart Granger war einer der schillerndsten Hollywood-Stars der 1950er Jahre – und gleichzeitig einer der einsamsten Männer seiner Generation. Seine Geschichte ist die Geschichte einer ganzen Ära des Kinos, die heute fast vergessen ist.

Zsa Zsa, Eva und Magda Gabor kamen aus Budapest und wurden in Amerika zu den ersten Stars, die vor allem für eines berühmt waren: dafür, berühmt zu sein – lange vor den Kardashians. Eine Geschichte über Glanz, falsche Adelstitel und den Preis dahinter.
